tool.name: Build HETEROFOR Forcing Files
tool.description: from SAFRAN reanalysis data regridded onto RENECOFOR plots, optionally completed with observed RENECOFOR data
tool.command: mkdir -p heterofor_safran_only #if str($reneco_cond.use_reneco) == "yes" && mkdir -p heterofor_combined #end if && Rscript '$__tool_directory__/build_heterofor_forcing.R' --safran_data '$safran_data' --psurf_data '$psurf_data' --stations '$stations' --wind_height_safran $wind_height_safran --wind_atten_coef $wind_atten_coef --out_safran_dir heterofor_safran_only #if str($reneco_cond.use_reneco) == "yes" --reneco_rds '$reneco_cond.reneco_rds' --safran_end_date '$reneco_cond.safran_end_date' --wind_height_combined $reneco_cond.wind_height_combined --out_combined_dir heterofor_combined --filling_summary '$filling_summary' --missing_summary '$missing_summary' #end if

param.name: safran_data
param.label: SAFRAN/ORCHIDEE forcing file
param.help: NetCDF, CSV, Parquet or CoverageJSON (auto-detected). See Help below for required columns.

param.name: psurf_data
param.label: SAFRAN/ORCHIDEE PSurf file
param.help: Surface pressure file, same accepted formats as above. See Help below.

param.name: stations
param.label: RENECOFOR station metadata
param.help: Tab-delimited file or RDS data.frame with a 'Station' column. See Help below for row-order requirements with NetCDF.

param.name: wind_height_safran
param.label: Wind speed measurement height for the SAFRAN-only files (m)
param.help: Written as 'windSpeedMeasurementHeight' in the header of the SAFRAN-only forcing files.

param.name: wind_atten_coef
param.label: Wind speed attenuation coefficient
param.help: Written as 'windSpeedAttenuationCoefficient' in the header of every forcing file produced.

param.name: use_reneco
param.label: Combine SAFRAN with observed RENECOFOR station data?
param.help: See Help below for details on the combined mode.
param.option: Yes, combine with observed RENECOFOR data

param.name: reneco_rds
param.label: Observed RENECOFOR meteorological data (RDS)
param.help: RDS data.frame, one row per station-hour. See Help below for the required column layout.

param.name: safran_end_date
param.label: Drop SAFRAN records at or after this date (UTC)

param.name: wind_height_combined
param.label: Wind speed measurement height for the combined files (m)
param.help: Written as 'windSpeedMeasurementHeight' in the combined file header.

tool.help:
What this tool does ====================
This tool builds hourly meteorological forcing files for the **HETEROFOR** forest growth model at the 26 plots of the **RENECOFOR** network, starting from **SAFRAN** reanalysis data (via the ORCHIDEE land surface model output format) that has already been regridded onto the RENECOFOR plot locations.
For every RENECOFOR station it writes one tab-delimited forcing file containing, per hour:
- Radiation (W/m2) - Air temperature (degC) - Soil surface temperature (degC, currently set equal to air temperature) - Rainfall (l/m2 or mm) - Relative humidity (%), derived from SAFRAN specific humidity, air temperature and surface pressure using the ECMWF water/ice saturation vapour pressure formula - Wind speed (m/s) - Wind direction (degrees, set to 0 when not available) - Diffuse to global radiation ratio (set to a constant 0.5)
Stations for which any value in any column is missing over the full period are left out of a given output set, and reported in the tool's log.
Two modes ---------
1. **SAFRAN-only** (default): forcing files are built entirely from the regridded SAFRAN/ORCHIDEE data, for every station present in the station metadata file.
2. **RENECOFOR + SAFRAN**: if you also supply an RDS file with observed RENECOFOR meteorological data, a second set of forcing files is produced per station, using RENECOFOR observations first and filling any gap with SAFRAN data. Radiation is always taken from SAFRAN (RENECOFOR radiation sensors are considered less reliable). The hourly record for each station starts on 1 January of the first year with RENECOFOR data for that station, and runs through the last available RENECOFOR record. Stations with no RENECOFOR data at all only appear in the SAFRAN-only output. Two extra tabular reports are produced in this mode:
- **SAFRAN-filling summary**: per station, the number and percentage of hours filled from SAFRAN, for each variable. - **missing-value summary**: per station, any values still missing after combining RENECOFOR and SAFRAN.
Observed RENECOFOR data (combined mode) ========================================
The optional RDS file must contain a data.frame with one row per station-hour and these columns: ``Station``, ``Year``, ``Month``, ``Day``, ``Hour``, ``Radiation``, ``Air_temperature``, ``Soil_surface_temperature``, ``Rainfall``, ``Relative_humidity``, ``Wind_speed``, ``Wind_direction``, ``Diffuse_to_global_ratio`` (the same layout as the SAFRAN-only output). RENECOFOR stations typically measure wind at 2 m, hence the different default wind measurement height in this mode compared to SAFRAN-only.
The "drop SAFRAN records at or after this date" option protects against known artefacts near the end of the SAFRAN record when combining it with RENECOFOR data; the default (2024-01-01) reflects the current known extent of reliable SAFRAN data at the time this tool was written.
Accepted formats for the SAFRAN and PSurf files ================================================
The two SAFRAN inputs accept **NetCDF, CSV, Parquet or CoverageJSON**; the format of each file is auto-detected from its content, independently of the other, so e.g. a CoverageJSON main file can be combined with a NetCDF PSurf file. Whichever format is used, both files must cover the same stations and the same hourly period.
**NetCDF** is expected to already be regridded onto the RENECOFOR plot locations, one value per plot per hour, e.g. with `Climate Data Operators (CDO) <https://code.mpimet.mpg.de/projects/cdo>`_::
# main variables (bilinear remapping) cdo -remapbil,station_grid.txt -delname,PSurf safran_input.nc safran_regridded.nc
# surface pressure (nearest-neighbour remapping; bilinear does not work # correctly for PSurf) cdo remapnn,station_grid.txt psurf_input.nc psurf_regridded.nc
``station_grid.txt`` is a CDO "cell" grid description file listing the longitude and latitude of each RENECOFOR plot, in the same order as the "Station" metadata file given to this tool. See the example test data for the expected file layout. With NetCDF, stations are matched to the metadata file **by position** (the order of the "ncells" dimension), not by name, so the station order must match exactly.
**CSV or Parquet** files must be in "long" format, one row per station per hour, with these columns:
- ``Station``: plot name, matched **by name** against the station metadata file (order does not matter with these formats) - ``Year``, ``Month``, ``Day``, ``Hour``: integer date/time components - for the main SAFRAN file: ``Tair`` (K), ``Qair`` (kg/kg), ``Wind`` (m/s), ``Rainf`` (kg/m2/s), ``Snowf`` (kg/m2/s), ``SWdown`` (W/m2), ``LWdown`` (W/m2) - for the PSurf file: ``PSurf`` (Pa)
These are the same variables, units and hourly time step as the NetCDF files above; note that these are **not** the daily variables (``T_Q``, ``FF_Q``, etc.) distributed by public daily SAFRAN-ISBA APIs such as GéoSAS, which cannot be used directly here (see below).
**CoverageJSON** files must be either a single `Coverage <https://covjson.org/>`_ object (one station) or a ``CoverageCollection`` (one ``Coverage`` per station, as GéoSAS's "cube" queries would produce for several plots). Each ``Coverage`` must have:
- an ``"id"`` field giving the station name, matched **by name** against the station metadata file (as with CSV/Parquet) - a ``domain.axes.t.values`` array of hourly timestamps, either standard ISO 8601 (``2024-01-01T00:00:00Z``) or the GéoSAS-style variant with hyphens instead of colons (``2024-01-01T00-00-00Z``) - for the main SAFRAN file, a ``ranges.<name>.values`` array (parallel to the time axis) for each of ``Tair``, ``Qair``, ``Wind``, ``Rainf``, ``Snowf``, ``SWdown``, ``LWdown``; for the PSurf file, ``ranges.PSurf``
As with CSV/Parquet, these ``ranges`` names and units must match the target variables above, not GéoSAS's own daily parameter codes.
A note on data sources: HETEROFOR's water balance, photosynthesis and (optional) phenology all run on an hourly time step, so this tool needs genuinely hourly meteorological data. Publicly available SAFRAN products such as the `GéoSAS SAFRAN-ISBA API <https://geosas.fr/web/?page_id=6345>`_ only distribute **daily** values, under different variable names, and cannot be plugged into this tool without a prior disaggregation step to hourly data, which this tool does not perform.
RENECOFOR station metadata ===========================
The station metadata can be given either as a tab-delimited text file or as an RDS file holding a data.frame (e.g. produced upstream in your own R pipeline with ``saveRDS()``); only a "Station" column is actually required, any other columns (such as Lon/Lat) are ignored.
Output collections ===================
Because the number of forcing files depends on how many stations pass the completeness check, outputs are returned as Galaxy **list collections** (one collection element per station), rather than as a fixed set of datasets.
Notes on this Galaxy wrapper =============================
This tool wraps a cleaned-up and parameterised version of an R script originally written by Annemiek I Stegehuis to prepare SAFRAN/RENECOFOR forcing data for HETEROFOR runs at the ALAMOD project plots. Compared to the original script, this version:
- reads all file paths and thresholds from command-line arguments instead of hard-coded local paths, so it can run inside Galaxy (or from the command line) on any input; - reads the observed RENECOFOR data from the RDS file given as input (the original script relied on this object already being present in the R session); - logs diagnostic information (relative humidity range, dropped stations, number of files written) to the job log instead of printing bare expressions to the console; - replaces a few non-ASCII placeholder characters in the forcing file header with plain-ASCII unit labels (e.g. "degC" instead of a stray "?"), for portability; - is organised into small, documented functions and passes R's `lintr` package (default linters: https://lintr.r-lib.org) with zero warnings.
The underlying meteorological calculations (unit conversions, the ECMWF-based specific-to-relative-humidity conversion, and the RENECOFOR/SAFRAN gap-filling logic) are unchanged from the original script.
